*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Darfur campaign (2023–present)|Darfur campaign]]
***The [[Rapid Support Forces]] state that they accept a humanitarian [[ceasefire]] proposed by international mediators after capturing [[El Fasher]] in [[Darfur]], while the [[Sudan]]ese [[Sudanese Armed Forces|army]] signals plans to continue the conflict. '''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Pacific typhoon season]]
**The death toll from [[Typhoon Kalmaegi]]'s impact on the [[Philippines]] rises to at least 142, with 127 others missing. The storm has left the [[Philippine Area of Responsibility|country's territory]] and made landfall in central [[Vietnam]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/11/6/typhoon-kalmaegi-bears-down-on-vietnam-after-114-killed-in-the-philippines (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Philippine president]] [[Bongbong Marcos]] declares a national [[State of calamity (Philippines)|state of calamity]] in relation to the devastation caused by Typhoon Kalmaegi and in anticipation of the upcoming [[tropical cyclone]] Fung-wong. [https://www.abs-cbn.com/news/nation/2025/11/6/marcos-oks-declaration-state-of-national-calamity-over-tino-upcoming-typhoon-1012 (ABS-CBN News)]
*At least three people are killed, two others are missing and two are presumed dead when a large structure being prepared for demolition at a [[power plant]] collapses in [[Ulsan]], [[South Korea]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/one-dead-south-korea-power-plant-collapse-safety-fears-hamper-rescue-2025-11-07/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2020–2025 H5N1 outbreak]]
**[[2025 Canadian ostrich culling controversy]]
***[[Canada]]'s [[Supreme Court of Canada|Supreme Court]] rejects an appeal by [[Universal Ostrich Farm]], allowing the [[Canadian Food Inspection Agency]] to carry out a full [[cull]] of nearly 400 [[ostrich]]es in [[Edgewood, British Columbia|Edgewood]], [[British Columbia]], under [[bird flu]] containment rules aligned with [[World Health Organization|WHO]] guidelines. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/world/canada-s-top-court-clears-path-for-culling-of-400-ostriches-amid-bird-flu-fears/3737931 (AA)]

'''International relations'''
*[[International sanctions against Syria]]
**The [[United Nations Security Council]] votes to lift sanctions on [[Syria]]n [[President of Syria|president]] [[Ahmed al-Sharaa]] and [[Ministry of Interior (Syria)|interior minister]] [[Anas Khattab]] through a [[United States and the United Nations|United States]]-drafted [[United Nations resolution|resolution]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/un-security-council-removes-sanctions-syrias-president-interior-minister-2025-11-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[Israel–Kazakhstan relations]] 
**[[Kazakhstan]] formally joins the [[Abraham Accords]], with the aim to enhance bilateral cooperation with [[Israel]]. [https://apnews.com/article/us-israel-kazakhstan-abraham-accords-5bf062712bd7bb326640bd78ba505d19 (AP)]
*[[Mexico–Peru relations]]
**[[Peru]]'s [[Congress of the Republic of Peru|Congress]] declares [[Mexico|Mexican]] [[President of Mexico|president]] [[Claudia Sheinbaum]] a ''[[persona non grata]]'' after Peru cut diplomatic ties with Mexico for granting [[Asylum seeker|asylum]] to former [[Prime Minister of Peru|prime minister]] [[Betssy Chávez]], who faces conspiracy charges related to former [[President of Peru|president]] [[Pedro Castillo]]'s attempt to dissolve Congress. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/peru-reviews-safe-passage-mexico-former-pm-holed-up-mexican-embassy-2025-11-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[Khaled El-Enany]] is elected director-general of [[UNESCO]] by the General Conference held in [[Samarkand]], [[Uzbekistan]], succeeding [[Audrey Azoulay]]. [https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/khaled-el-enany-elected-director-general-unesco (UNESCO)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2019 Bolivian political crisis]]
**Former [[Bolivia]]n [[President of Bolivia|president]] [[Jeanine Áñez]] is freed from [[Prisons in Bolivia|prison]] after the [[Supreme Tribunal of Justice of Bolivia|Supreme Court]] annulled her sentence the previous day. [https://apnews.com/article/jeanine-anez-bolivia-prison-ca6625b53c6ebdab7c44f8809f73035d (AP)]
*[[Crime in Germany]]
**The [[Hesse State Police]] announce an investigation in [[Hanau]] after [[swastika]]s made of human [[blood]] are found painted on dozens of buildings and cars. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/dozens-swastikas-painted-human-blood-daubed-property-german-127247445 (AP via ABC News)]
*[[International Criminal Court investigation in Uganda]]
**The [[International Criminal Court]] confirms 39 charges of [[war crime]]s and [[crimes against humanity]] against fugitive [[Lord's Resistance Army]] leader [[Joseph Kony]] [[Trial in absentia|in absentia]], including murder, rape, [[sexual slavery]], [[forced pregnancy]], and the use of [[Child soldiers in Uganda|child soldiers]]. The court rules that he can stand trial once arrested, upholding the [[List of people indicted in the International Criminal Court#Joseph Kony|2005 arrest warrant]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/icc-confirms-war-crimes-charges-against-ugandas-kony-2025-11-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[Murder of Agnes Wanjiru]]
**A former [[British Army|British soldier]], Robert James Purkiss, is arrested on a [[Kenya]]n [[extradition]] warrant related to Agnes Wanjiru's 2012 murder near a [[British Army Training Unit Kenya|UK military training]] facility in [[Nanyuki]], [[Laikipia County]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/11/7/former-british-soldier-contests-extradition-over-alleged-kenya-murder (Al Jazeera)]
*[[War crimes in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|War crimes in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**A [[Judiciary of Russia|court]] in [[Russian-occupied territories of Ukraine|Russian-occupied]] [[Donetsk People's Republic|Donetsk]] sentences two [[Colombians]] to 13 years in [[Prisons in Russia|prison]] for fighting with [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukraine's armed forces]], after they were detained while traveling [[Colombia|home]] through [[Venezuela]] and transferred into Russian custody. [https://www.kyivpost.com/post/63800 (AFP via ''Kyiv Post'')]
**A [[Judiciary of Ukraine|court]] in [[Zaporizhzhia]], [[Ukraine]], finds a [[Russia]]n [[Russian Armed Forces|soldier]] guilty of killing a [[Prisoner of war|surrendered]] [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian soldier]] in January 2024 and sentences him to [[life imprisonment]], marking the first conviction of a Russian soldier for killing a captured Ukrainian since [[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|the war]] began. [https://edition.cnn.com/2025/11/06/europe/russian-soldier-guilty-killing-ukrainian-prisoner-intl (CNN)]
